content.title: About
content.content: Almond milk is a plant‑based beverage made by blending almonds with water and straining the mixture. It has a mild nutty flavor, a light‑cream color, and is often used as a dairy‑free alternative.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Almond milk contains roughly 3‑5 times fewer calories than whole cow’s milk.
Commercial production of almond milk began in the United States in the 1990s.
In the U.S., almond milk has become the most popular plant milk, surpassing soy.
About 100 g of almonds are needed to produce 1 L of milk.
Almond milk is naturally lactose‑free, gluten‑free, and soy‑free.

items.title: Rich in vitamin E
items.content: Vitamin E is a powerful antioxidant that supports skin health and the immune system.

items.title: Low in sugar
items.content: Unsweetened almond milk contains very little natural sugar, making it suitable for low‑carb diets.

items.title: Source of healthy fats
items.content: Almonds provide monounsaturated fatty acids that help maintain cardiovascular health.

items.title: Supports bone health
items.content: Fortified versions often contain calcium and vitamin D, nutrients essential for strong bones.

items.title: Easy to digest
items.content: Being lactose‑free, it is safe for people with lactose intolerance.

items.title: Tree nut allergy
items.content: Individuals allergic to almonds may experience reactions when consuming almond milk.

items.title: Low protein content
items.content: Compared with cow’s milk, almond milk provides significantly less protein.

items.title: Added sugars
items.content: Flavored varieties can contain added sugars, increasing calorie count.

items.title: Oxalates
items.content: Almonds contain oxalates; people prone to kidney stones should limit intake.

content.title: How to Use
content.content: Almond milk can be enjoyed on its own, added to coffee, smoothies, cereals, baked goods, or used in sauces. For a richer texture, choose unsweetened, full‑fat versions.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store opened almond milk in the refrigerator at 1‑4 °C and consume within 5‑7 days. Do not freeze, as the texture may separate.

infant-formula-enfamil-gentlease-powder-.title: Infant formula, Enfamil Gentlease, powder, prepared with bottled water

content.title: About
content.content: Enfamil Gentlease is an infant formula powder designed for babies from birth to 12 months with sensitive digestion. It contains partially hydrolyzed proteins, probiotics, and an optimal blend of vitamins and minerals. Preparation uses bottled water to ensure a consistent composition and safety.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Gentlease features partially hydrolyzed proteins that reduce the likelihood of colic and gas.
The formula is enriched with DHA and ARA, fatty acids important for brain and eye development.
Prebiotic fibers (FOS) are included to support the growth of beneficial gut bacteria.
Enfamil Gentlease has undergone clinical trials confirming its hypoallergenic properties.
Each sachet is calibrated to make a 30 ml serving with 7 g of powder.

items.title: Digestive comfort
items.content: Partially hydrolyzed proteins are easier to break down, lowering the risk of colic and constipation in infants.

items.title: Brain development
items.content: DHA and ARA support neuronal connections and visual function.

items.title: Immune support
items.content: Vitamins A, C, E and zinc help strengthen the baby’s immune system.

items.title: Healthy gut flora
items.content: Prebiotics promote beneficial bacteria, improving nutrient absorption.

items.title: Optimal growth
items.content: Balanced calcium, phosphorus and magnesium contribute to proper bone and teeth formation.

items.title: Milk protein allergy
items.content: Infants with a confirmed cow‑milk protein allergy should use a dedicated hypoallergenic formula.

items.title: Incorrect dilution
items.content: Over‑concentrated formula can cause dehydration, while overly dilute mixes may lack essential nutrients.

items.title: Storage after opening
items.content: Keep the container tightly sealed in a dry place, away from moisture and light.

items.title: Water temperature control
items.content: Use boiled water cooled to 40 °C – 50 °C; water that is too hot destroys sensitive nutrients.

content.title: How to Prepare
content.content: Sterilize the bottle, add 7 g of powder to 30 ml of prepared bottled water (40 °C – 50 °C), shake vigorously until fully dissolved. Use the prepared feed within one hour.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the dry powder in its original packaging in a cool, dry place protected from direct sunlight. Once opened, use within 30 days.

content.title: About
content.content: Lasagna with meat and spinach is a layered Italian dish made of pasta sheets, ground meat, fresh spinach, tomato sauce, and cheese. When baked, the ingredients meld into a fragrant, hearty, and nutritious meal.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Traditional lasagna is built in multiple layers, and adding spinach makes it greener and more nutrient‑dense.
The meat is usually beef or pork mince, but turkey or chicken can be used for a lighter version.
Spinach is rich in iron and B‑vitamins, boosting blood health and energy metabolism.
In Italy, lasagna is often served at celebrations and family gatherings, with regional variations adding local ingredients.
Cheese commonly combines mozzarella for stretchiness and Parmesan for flavor.

items.title: Rich source of protein
items.content: Meat and cheese provide high‑quality protein essential for muscle growth and repair.

items.title: Contains iron
items.content: Spinach and meat supply iron, important for oxygen transport in the blood.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: The dish offers B6, B12, and folate, supporting metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Calcium and vitamin D
items.content: Cheese adds calcium and a modest amount of vitamin D, promoting bone health.

items.title: Dietary fiber
items.content: Spinach and tomato sauce contribute fiber, aiding digestion.

items.title: High calorie content
items.content: Lasagna is rich in fats and carbohydrates, so portion control is advisable, especially on weight‑loss diets.

items.title: Sodium levels
items.content: Tomato sauce and cheese can be salty; people with hypertension should opt for low‑sodium versions.

items.title: Dairy allergy
items.content: Cheese may trigger reactions in individuals with lactose intolerance or milk allergy.

items.title: Meat safety
items.content: Undercooked meat can harbor harmful bacteria; ensure the mince is fully cooked.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve lasagna hot, cut into portion‑size squares. It pairs well with a simple green salad or steamed vegetables. Leftovers reheat well in the oven or microwave.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store cooked lasagna in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. For longer storage, freeze in portion‑sized bags for up to 2 months. Reheat until the internal temperature reaches 75 °C.

content.title: About
content.content: Mustard greens (Brassica juncea) are edible leafy vegetables belonging to the cruciferous family. When cooked they have a tender, slightly bitter flavor and a soft texture. They are common in Asian cuisines, used in salads, soups, and side dishes.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Mustard greens are rich in glucosinolates, which convert during cooking into compounds with anti‑inflammatory effects.
In traditional Chinese medicine they are used to aid digestion and support liver detoxification.
The seeds that produce mustard powder come from the same species, but the leaves are a distinct culinary product.
Mustard greens grow quickly and can be harvested 30‑40 days after sowing.
In Japan they are known as “mento” and are often served pickled.

items.title: High in vitamins A and C
items.content: Vitamin A supports vision and immunity, while vitamin C boosts antioxidant protection.

items.title: Source of calcium and iron
items.content: Calcium is essential for bone health, and iron is needed for oxygen transport in the blood.

items.title: Contains dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber aids digestion and promotes a feeling of fullness.

items.title: Rich in phytochemicals
items.content: Glucosinolates and carotenoids have anti‑cancer and anti‑inflammatory properties.

items.title: Low‑calorie food
items.content: One cup of cooked mustard greens provides about 25 kcal, making it an excellent choice for weight‑controlled diets.

items.title: Cruciferous allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions such as skin rash or swelling.

items.title: High oxalate content
items.content: People prone to kidney stones should limit intake.

items.title: Cooking considerations
items.content: Overcooking can reduce certain vitamins, so brief blanching is recommended.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Add mustard greens to salads, soups, stews, or serve as a side dish with meat or fish. They are usually blanched for 2‑3 minutes and then shocked in cold water to retain bright color and a slight crunch.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store cooked mustard greens in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. When frozen, they keep well for up to 2 months if packed in portion‑size bags.

pasta-with-tomato-based-sauce-cheese-and.title: Pasta with Tomato-Based Sauce, Cheese and Meat

content.title: About
content.content: Pasta with tomato-based sauce, cheese and meat is a ready‑to‑eat dish consisting of boiled pasta, coated with a tomato sauce, sprinkled with grated cheese and mixed with pieces of cooked or fried meat. The meal combines carbohydrates, protein and fat, providing a balanced source of energy.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Tomato sauce is often made from ripe tomatoes, olive oil, onion and herbs, making it a rich source of lycopene.
The tradition of pairing pasta with meat dates back to 19th‑century Italy, when meat ragù became popular.
Cheese added to the dish is usually Parmesan or mozzarella, giving it aroma and boosting calcium content.
Pasta cooks quickly: most shapes reach al dente in 8‑12 minutes after the water boils.
In restaurants the dish is commonly served as “spaghetti Bolognese,” though home cooks use any pasta shape.

items.title: Energy supply
items.content: The combination of carbs from pasta and protein from meat provides sustained satiety and supports energy levels.

items.title: Rich in lysine
items.content: Meat supplies lysine, an essential amino acid important for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Lycopene in tomatoes
items.content: Tomatoes contain lycopene, a powerful antioxidant that may protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Calcium from cheese
items.content: Grated cheese adds calcium, essential for bone and tooth health.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Enriched pasta and meat provide B1, B3 and B6 vitamins, supporting metabolism.

items.title: High calorie content
items.content: Because the dish combines carbs, fats and proteins, it can be calorie‑dense; portion control is advisable for weight management.

items.title: Sodium level
items.content: Tomato sauce and cheese often contain added salt, which may be a concern for people with hypertension.

items.title: Dairy allergy
items.content: Cheese can trigger allergic reactions in individuals with lactose intolerance or milk protein allergy.

items.title: Saturated fat
items.content: Meat and cheese may contain saturated fats, which in excess can raise cholesterol levels.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the dish hot, optionally topping with extra cheese and fresh herbs. A drizzle of olive oil or a pinch of spices can be added to taste. It pairs well with bread or a side salad for a balanced meal.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep cooked pasta in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. For longer storage, freeze it in a freezer‑safe bag for up to 2 months after cooling.

content.title: About
content.content: Iced bottled tea is a ready‑to‑drink beverage made from black tea that has undergone decaffeination and subsequent cooling. It is packaged in a sealed glass or plastic bottle, providing a long shelf life without added preservatives.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Decaffeination of black tea is usually performed with solvent or carbon‑dioxide methods, preserving most of the flavor notes.
Iced bottled tea is especially popular in warm climates where consumers seek refreshing non‑alcoholic drinks.
Black tea retains polyphenols even after decaffeination and cooling, contributing to its health profile.
Dark‑colored glass bottles better protect the drink from light‑induced oxidation, preserving aroma longer.
In some markets the tea is flavored with natural additives such as lemon or mint.

items.title: Rich in antioxidants
items.content: Black tea contains polyphenols that help neutralize free radicals and support cellular health.

items.title: Supports cardiovascular health
items.content: Moderate regular consumption of black tea may improve vessel function and lower LDL cholesterol.

items.title: Hydration aid
items.content: Caffeine‑free iced tea is a pleasant way to maintain fluid balance, especially on hot days.

items.title: Stress reduction
items.content: The amino acid L‑theanine in tea promotes relaxation without causing drowsiness.

items.title: Digestive support
items.content: Black tea can help stimulate gastric motility and aid digestion.

items.title: Tea allergy
items.content: A small number of individuals may experience allergic reactions to tea components.

items.title: Tannin content
items.content: Tannins can reduce absorption of certain minerals such as iron when consumed in large amounts.

items.title: Added sugars or sweeteners
items.content: Some versions contain added sugar or artificial sweeteners, which should be considered in dietary planning.

items.title: Plastic packaging
items.content: Long‑term storage in plastic may allow trace chemical migration; glass bottles are preferable.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the tea chilled straight from the bottle. For extra flavor, add a slice of lemon, a sprig of mint, or a few berries.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the bottle in a cool, dark place away from direct sunlight. Once opened, refrigerate and consume within 3–5 days.

content.title: About
content.content: Upma is a traditional South Indian dish made from semolina (suji) that is steamed with spices, vegetables, and sometimes legumes. The dish has a soft, slightly fluffy texture and is flavored with aromatic herbs such as mustard seeds, curry leaves, and turmeric.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Upma is commonly eaten for breakfast, but it can be enjoyed at any time of day.
There are many regional variations: Kerala adds coconut milk, Andhra Pradesh includes lentils, and Tamil Nadu incorporates nuts and dried fruits.
The dish is considered light and easily digestible, making it a frequent choice for the sick and for children.
Traditionally upma is cooked in a special steam pot (uruli), but it can also be prepared in a regular skillet.
The semolina used in upma is rich in carbohydrates and provides a quick source of energy.

items.title: Source of complex carbs
items.content: Semolina releases glucose slowly, helping to maintain stable blood sugar levels.

items.title: Rich in B‑vitamins
items.content: Upma contains thiamine, riboflavin, and niacin, which support energy metabolism.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Because it uses modest amounts of oil, the dish fits well into low‑fat dietary plans.

items.title: Contains dietary fiber
items.content: Added vegetables and legumes increase fiber content, aiding digestion.

items.title: Antioxidant spices
items.content: Turmeric and mustard seeds have anti‑inflammatory and antioxidant properties.

items.title: Gluten allergy
items.content: Semolina is made from wheat, so people with celiac disease should use gluten‑free alternatives.

items.title: High glycemic index
items.content: Large portions of upma can raise blood sugar quickly.

items.title: Salt and oil content
items.content: Recipes often call for generous amounts of oil and salt, which may be unsuitable for hypertension.

items.title: Spicy ingredients
items.content: Some versions include hot chilies that can irritate the stomach of sensitive individuals.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve hot upma with chutney, yogurt, or coconut sauce. Garnish with toasted nuts, fresh herbs, and a squeeze of lime for extra flavor. A “plain” version can be made without oil, using vegetable broth instead.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep cooked upma in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3 days. Reheat in a skillet with a splash of water or oil to restore its soft texture.
